## Context

Branches created before cutover can still contain local ledger writes.
Import those events once and preserve code changes without tracker merge conflicts.
The owner-approved layout uses a file guard and a complete frozen archive.
Earlier directory-marker and registry designs remain in record history.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py`
- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/arguments.py`
- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/REFERENCE.md`
- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/vault_migrate_branch.py`
- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/code_audit.py`
- `tests/test_kit_vault_migrate_branch.py`
- `changelog.d/basicly-gtb19bg.43.22.added.md`

## Plan

- depends on: `S5a: audit the code default branch with fsck --code and store link and miss events`, `V5: migrate a ledger, beads, br or beans backlog into a vault and export it back`, `Repair the complete write lifecycle for vault-born records`, `Prevent unsafe writes across engine and kit generations`
- demonstration: `python3 .basicly/core/kit/tracker/cli.py migrate --branch --vault vault.git` imports missing events before the branch merges without tracker conflicts.

payload.name: acceptance_criteria
payload.value:
- When migrate --branch runs on a branch cut before the freeze, the tracker shall import its post-freeze ledger lines by event id and remove its ledger changes in one commit on that branch.
- When a branch with .basicly/ledger changes lands on the code default branch after cutover, the next fsck --code shall import each new ledger line by event id.
- When an imported event id is already valid in the vault, the import shall skip it.
- Proof T-branch: input a branch cut before the freeze that appends to .basicly/ledger; action migrate --branch on it, then merge it; pass when the merge has no conflict and each line is in the vault once.
- Proof T-late-ledger: input a branch merged after cutover that adds a new pending ledger shard; action fsck --code twice; pass when the first run imports each line once and the second imports nothing.
- Cutover shall preserve every original ledger byte in .basicly/ledger-archive/.
- migrate --branch shall import every missing ledger event by id.
- After cutover, a new write to the old ledger on the default branch shall be refused, naming the vault command.
- Proof T-old-ledger-refused: input a cut-over fixture; action a tracker write against the old ledger on the default branch; pass when it exits refused and names the vault command.
- During active cutover, raw events.append writes to the guard or frozen archive shall refuse with exit code 2.
- The refusal shall name the vault command.
- After validated per-repository rollback from current canonical export, normal local ledger writes shall succeed.
- Cutover shall create a tracked regular-file guard at .basicly/ledger.
- The guard shall identify the vault move and frozen archive without changing original ledger bytes.
- fsck shall report the frozen archive and name removal record basicly-9f4legn.
- Session start, fsck and the board shall read the vault after cutover.
- Proof T-frozen-marker: input a cut-over fixture and a branch cut before cutover that appends to a ledger shard; action merge that branch, then fsck --code and fsck; pass when the merge has no conflict, each line is in the vault once, and fsck names the frozen ledger and the removal record.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
- When installed with either distribution, tracker-owned vault clones shall receive the same push guard automatically.
- When a protected clone pushes, the guard shall validate every outgoing commit and ref update.
- When a push changes unexpected paths or invalid events, it shall refuse before remote history changes.
- When a push deletes or rewrites history, creates another branch, or pushes tags, it shall refuse.
- When tracker batches are valid, normal concurrent sharing and retries shall still succeed.
- When protection is requested for an existing vault clone, installation shall preserve unrelated hooks or refuse without changes.
- When installed or updated, protection shall remain usable on Windows, Linux, and macOS without another hook dependency.
- When pushed through the tracker, validation shall run without disabling hooks.
- When a code repository pushes ordinary code, vault-specific restrictions shall not apply.
- When installation or validation fails, queued events and existing repository files shall remain intact.
- When a manually cloned vault lacks protection, guidance shall name the explicit protection command.
payload.description:
## Context

The owner wants accidental agent and human pushes rejected before they add unrelated files to backlog-vault.
The standalone tracker and basicly must install and maintain protection with little setup.
Existing commit quarantine only controls accepted tracker history after a push.
It does not prevent unwanted Git objects or refs from reaching the remote.
Current vault_share._push also selects an empty hooks directory.
Replace that override with the reviewed tracker guard rather than bypassing protection.

## Scope

- Tracker kit push validation and hook installation.
- Automatic protection for tracker-owned clones and explicit protection for manual clones.
- Standalone and harness guidance and cross-platform consumer checks.

## Plan

- demonstration: `uv run pytest tests/test_kit_vault_push_guard.py tests/test_kit_vault_push_guard_consumer.py tests/test_kit_vault_share.py tests/test_kit_vault_cli_wiring.py -q` proves valid sharing and refused malformed pushes against fixture remotes.
payload.requirements: Share one validator and installer across standalone and harness distributions. Use Git native hooks and the existing Python runtime. Add no dependency. Never modify global Git configuration. Preserve caller-owned hooks and repository files. Demonstrate refusal with unchanged actual remote refs. Local hooks prevent accidents; deliberately bypassed hooks and server policy enforcement are separate boundaries. Remote settings need separate owner approval.
payload.title: Reject accidental non-tracker pushes from vault clones
